backlog.spec: After the first SLSQP restart, keep the best packing found so far. Each later iteration copies the best packing, moves 1 to 3 randomly chosen circles to new uniform random positions (or jitters all centres by N(0, 0.03)), re-runs _solve_once from that perturbed start, repairs, and keeps the result only if its radius sum is larger. Use the same time budget and the seed-driven rng.
backlog.title: Basin hopping from the incumbent

backlog.spec: Once a valid best packing exists, repeatedly take the circle with the smallest radius, delete it, and reinsert it at the point that maximises the distance to all other circles and walls (estimate by evaluating a 200x200 grid of candidate points and taking the max of min(distance to centres minus radii, distance to walls)). Re-optimise with SLSQP from this start, repair, and keep if improved.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert smallest circle

backlog.spec: Pass a jac argument to minimize for both the objective and the constraint function. The objective gradient is -1 on the radius entries and 0 on the centre entries. The constraint Jacobian is built with numpy: for each pair row, derivatives with respect to the two centres and two radii of the unit-direction vector and the -1 terms; for wall rows, the constant +1 or -1 entries. This removes finite-difference cost so more restarts fit in the time budget and each run converges more tightly.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobians for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Instead of all n(n-1)/2 pair constraints, build the pair list only for pairs whose centres are within a threshold (for example 2.2 times the current typical radius, about 0.4) at the start of each SLSQP call, and keep those pairs fixed for that call. Re-check after the run whether any excluded pair overlaps and, if so, add those pairs and run SLSQP once more. This shrinks the constraint matrix and speeds each iteration.
backlog.title: Sparse neighbour constraints

backlog.spec: For each restart, first minimise a smooth penalty objective with L-BFGS-B: maximise the radius sum minus mu times the squared violations of pair and wall constraints, with mu increased over 4 stages (1e2, 1e3, 1e4, 1e5). Then use the resulting centres and radii as the start for SLSQP with the exact constraints. The penalty stage is cheap and gives SLSQP a near-feasible start, reducing failed or slow SLSQP runs.
backlog.title: Two-stage optimisation: penalty then SLSQP

backlog.spec: Keep the random-restart SLSQP stage, but for the best candidate found, run scipy.optimize.minimize with method='trust-constr' using the same objective and nonlinear constraint (lower bound 0, upper bound inf), with maxiter 500. Accept the trust-constr result only if it is valid after repair and has a larger radius sum than the SLSQP result. Trust-constr often converges to tighter KKT points on packing problems.
backlog.title: Switch to trust-constr for polishing

backlog.spec: Raise MAX_ITER from 200 to 1000 and set options ftol to 1e-12 in SLSQP. Many random starts currently stop at 200 iterations before converging, so the reported radius sum is below the local optimum. A larger cap with a tight tolerance gives each start a fair chance to reach its local optimum.
backlog.title: Increase SLSQP iteration cap and add a convergence tolerance

backlog.spec: Run a large pool of random restarts with a low iteration cap (for example 40 SLSQP iterations) and rank them by radius sum after repair. Keep only the top 20 percent and continue optimising them with the full cap of 500 iterations. Repeat the keep-top-fraction step once more if time allows. This spends most of the budget on promising starts.
backlog.title: Successive halving over restarts

backlog.spec: Divide the 0.8 * time_limit budget into two phases. The first 40 percent runs independent random restarts and records the best. The last 60 percent runs only local perturbation-and-reoptimise steps around the best packing found, with perturbation scale shrinking linearly from 0.05 to 0.005 over that phase. Use time.process_time to decide when each phase ends.
backlog.title: Time-split between exploration and exploitation

backlog.spec: In a basin-hopping loop around the best packing, the perturbation standard deviation for centre positions decreases geometrically from 0.08 at the start of the budget to 0.002 at the end, following the fraction of time used. Each step jitters centres with that scale, re-optimises with SLSQP, repairs, and accepts only improvements. The schedule is a function of time.process_time() elapsed over the budget.
backlog.title: Annealed perturbation scale

backlog.spec: Track the radius sum of each restart. If the last 10 restarts have not improved on the best, switch from uniform random initial centres to perturbations of the current best (jitter 0.05) for the next 10 restarts; otherwise keep the random-start mode. Alternate the modes according to this rule until the time budget ends.
backlog.title: Adaptive restart scheduling by improvement rate

backlog.spec: Generate some starting points from a hexagonal or square lattice with spacing chosen so that 26 points fit inside [0.1, 0.9]^2: choose the lattice with the number of points closest to n, drop extra points at random, and add Gaussian noise of 0.02. Alternate these starts with uniform random starts. Lattice starts give SLSQP structured configurations close to good packings.
backlog.title: Hexagonal-lattice initial layouts

backlog.spec: Build an initial configuration sequentially: place the first circle at a random point, then for each new circle evaluate a 100x100 grid over the square and choose the point maximising min(distance to existing centres minus their current radii, distance to walls), with radius set to that value times 0.9. Use this greedy packing as the SLSQP start for a fraction of the restarts. It produces starts with varied, reasonable radii.
backlog.title: Greedy largest-hole initialisation

backlog.spec: Replace the constant initial radius 0.05 with radii drawn from a uniform distribution between 0.02 and 0.12 using rng, then rescale all radii so that the sum of areas equals 0.6 of the unit square. This gives starts with mixed sizes, which is the structure of many good packings with unequal radii, and lets SLSQP explore a broader set of basins.
backlog.title: Random initial radii drawn from a distribution

backlog.spec: For each restart, first solve a reduced problem where all radii are forced equal to a single variable r, maximising r subject to the pair and wall constraints (2n+1 variables). Use the resulting centres and r as the initial point for the full SLSQP with unequal radii. The equal-radius problem is smaller and converges quickly, giving a good starting configuration.
backlog.title: Equal-radius warm start

backlog.spec: Optionally restrict a fraction of restarts to configurations symmetric about the diagonal y = x: optimise only half the centres, mirror each to (y, x), and duplicate radii. Pairs that are mirror images of each other are then fixed to be symmetric. Run SLSQP on this reduced problem, then unfold the solution and run one unrestricted SLSQP polish from it. Symmetric configurations are a large share of best-known packings.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric search space

backlog.spec: Initialise the restart with the 4 corner regions occupied by circles placed at the corners and along the edges with radius chosen by the wall constraint, and only optimise the interior circles. Then run the full SLSQP from this start with all variables free. Fixing a boundary frame reduces the search space to the interior and matches the structure of tight packings near the walls.
backlog.title: Dimension-reduced search via fixed boundary circles

backlog.spec: Maintain an elite pool of the best 8 packings found. For each new restart, with probability 0.5 build a child by taking the centres with x < 0.5 from one parent and the centres with x >= 0.5 from another parent, fixing the count to n by adding or removing circles at random positions. Start SLSQP from the child. Replace the worst pool member when the child's repaired radius sum beats it.
backlog.title: Population with crossover of centre sets

backlog.spec: Stack a batch of 16 candidate configurations as one numpy array and evaluate the penalty objective and its gradient for all of them at once with vectorised numpy, using L-BFGS-B on the concatenated vector with block-diagonal independence (use the sum of the per-candidate losses as the objective). Keep the best 4 after the penalty stage and polish each with SLSQP. This amortises Python overhead across candidates.
backlog.title: Mini-batch of perturbed starts averaged by vectorised penalty

backlog.spec: Before running SLSQP, generate 200 random starts and score each with a fast feasibility-based estimate: run 30 iterations of a penalty gradient descent with numpy only, then compute the repaired radius sum. Pass only the top 3 starts to full SLSQP. This batch screening spends the time on the starts most likely to end in a good basin.
backlog.title: Evaluate many cheap starts before any SLSQP

backlog.spec: Run restarts in interleaved batches of 5: for each batch, create 5 starts, run SLSQP on all 5 in sequence with a shared iteration cap, and then continue only the best 2 in the next batch. Batching keeps the rng consumption deterministic and reduces the number of SLSQP calls that never improve the best.
backlog.title: Parallel-style multistart within one thread

backlog.spec: Before each SLSQP call, add Gaussian noise with standard deviation 0.01 to every centre and clip to [r, 1-r] for the initial radii. This regularisation keeps the optimiser out of symmetric saddle points that random uniform starts often converge to, and encourages it to leave flat regions where the constraint gradients are degenerate.
backlog.title: Jitter-based regularisation of the SLSQP start

backlog.spec: Add a small regulariser to the SLSQP objective: minus the radius sum plus 1e-4 times the sum of squared differences between each radius and the mean radius. This pushes SLSQP toward configurations with more even radii early in optimisation, avoiding tiny circles that trap the optimiser; set the weight to zero in a final polish stage so the true objective is optimised at the end.
backlog.title: Radius-sum penalty on small circles

backlog.spec: Replace the global shrink in _repair with an exact per-pair scaling: after the pair loop, for every violated pair shrink only the two radii by the minimum factor needed, iterating until no pair violates by more than 1e-13, and drop SHRINK to 1e-12. The harness tolerance is 1e-10, so the current 1e-9 margin wastes about 1e-9 times 26 of radius sum; a smaller margin keeps the result valid while recovering the slack.
backlog.title: Tighter repair to recover slack

backlog.spec: After the best packing is chosen, for each circle in turn, increase its radius to the largest value that keeps it inside the walls and not overlapping any other circle given the current radii, processing circles in order of decreasing radius. Repeat the sweep until no radius changes by more than 1e-12. This is a cheap post-processing step that often recovers a small amount of radius sum that the repair step left unused.
backlog.title: Final greedy radius inflation

backlog.spec: Inside each SLSQP call, use a callback to read the current iterate every 20 iterations. If the current radius sum is more than 0.15 below the best value found so far, stop that restart immediately by raising a custom exception caught in solve. Hopeless starts then no longer use the time budget, so more starts are tried within the 30 s limit.
backlog.title: Kill hopeless restarts early

backlog.spec: Estimate the average wall-clock cost of one SLSQP call from the first two restarts. Set the per-restart MAX_ITER so that roughly 25 restarts fit in the budget, clipped to the range 100 to 600. Recompute after every 5 restarts. This adapts the depth of each local search to the machine speed rather than using a fixed constant.
backlog.title: Use time.process_time-based adaptive iteration cap

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop around the current packing, accept a new local optimum even when its radius sum is lower, with probability exp((new - current) / T), where T starts at 0.01 and decays linearly to 0.0001 over the time budget. Keep a separate record of the best packing ever seen and return that one. This Metropolis-style acceptance lets the search escape local optima.
backlog.title: Stochastic acceptance of worse packings
